claim: Isolating multiple LVT units that all share the 10.0.1.0/24 subnet requires one VRF per unit plus source-NAT on the MikroTik hEX — VLANs alone leave colliding L3 connected routes, and source-NATting the initiator (Thor) to an L2-local address like 10.0.1.202 is mandatory when the devices' default gateway (cell modem) can't be changed.
trigger: when multiple physical networks must carry the same subnet through one router
before configuring MikroTik hEX routing for duplicate-subnet LVT units
when device replies vanish toward a cell-modem gateway you cannot change

claim: UniFi auto-channel selection runs independently per AP with no same-site coordination, so multi-AP sites often end with two APs on the same 5 GHz channel — pin channels manually by setting an integer channel in radio_table via PUT /api/s/default/rest/device/{_id}.
trigger: when two UniFi APs at one site land on the same 5 GHz channel
before deploying more than one UniFi AP at a site
when a manually set channel reverts after a day while the radio is still on channel 'auto'

claim: In UniFi's legacy /api/s/default/stat/sta client objects, the rate fields bytes-r, rx_bytes-r and tx_bytes-r are bytes per second — reading them as KB/s or Mbps inflates client traffic by 1000x and causes false streaming alarms.
trigger: when reading any UniFi *-r rate field from stat/sta
when a UniFi client's traffic rate looks implausibly high for an idle device

claim: A UniFi client with hostname 'audiocast' and Huizhou Gaoshengda OUI 24:3f:75 is an embedded WiFi/Chromecast audio module (on this network a JBL soundbar) — the hostname does not identify the actual product, so ask what audio gear the user owns; idle rate of 5-10 Kbps is normal keepalive, not streaming.
trigger: when an unknown device with hostname 'audiocast' appears on a UniFi network
when a client MAC OUI resolves to Huizhou Gaoshengda 24:3f:75

claim: A networking session summary records three UniFi learnings: same-site APs do not coordinate auto-channel selection, the bytes-r API field is bytes/sec not KB/s, and hostname 'audiocast' with Gaoshengda OUI 24:3f:75 marks an embedded WiFi-audio module rather than the product name.
trigger: when tracing which session recorded the UniFi auto-channel, bytes-r, or audiocast learnings

claim: A WiFiman AR heatmap is a recorded survey of only the AP the phone is currently associated with, so an unchanged heatmap after adding an AP usually means the phone never roamed — on the Lemmons network because LemmonsMain was pinned tx_power_mode='high' — and the fix is revert TX to auto, force re-association next to the new AP, then walk a fresh scan.
trigger: when a WiFiman heatmap looks unchanged after installing a new AP
when phones cling to the main AP instead of roaming to a closer one

claim: A session note records that learning_cf4fa70a8f8c1588 was stored: a WiFiman heatmap reflects only the currently-associated AP, so an unchanged map after adding an AP usually means the phone stayed stuck on the old high-TX-power AP.
trigger: when tracing which session recorded the WiFiman heatmap learning

claim: U7 Mesh install checkout found three gotchas: a UniFi UI TX-power edit can apply to only a subset of radios (LemmonsMain kept ng/na=high with only 6e changed to auto), DFS pins like ch100/ch52 show the old running channel for ~2 minutes during the CAC radar dwell so an early check falsely looks like a failed pin, and U7 Outdoor silently regressed to a wireless mesh uplink (5 GHz forced to follow LemmonsMain) after a suspected mower-cut cable.
trigger: after changing tx_power_mode through the UniFi UI
when a DFS channel pin still shows the old running channel within ~2 minutes
when an AP's uplink_type unexpectedly shows wireless

claim: A UniFi AP that falls back to a wireless mesh uplink retains its configured radio_table channel pin and auto-restores it when wired backhaul returns (verified on Shop Outdoor ch149 after its cut run was repaired), so plan no manual re-pin — just fix the wire; also tx_power_mode 'medium' is more deterministic than 'auto' for forcing client roaming, since auto kept the 5 GHz radio at 26 dBm.
trigger: when an AP that lost wired backhaul gets re-wired
before planning a manual channel re-pin for a mesh-uplinked AP
when tx_power_mode 'auto' keeps radiated power high after reverting from high

claim: A session note records that learning_25a74bab23058ac3 (TX partial-apply gotcha, DFS CAC lag, mesh regression) and learning_626396c1740260f5 (mesh-uplinked AP auto-restores its channel pin on re-wire; medium beats auto for roaming) were stored in a pure ops/config session.
trigger: when tracing which session recorded the U7 Mesh checkout and re-wire learnings
